newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Australia plans full pipeline sale - paper.
newsitem.headline: Western Australia plans full pipeline sale - paper.

text.p: The Western Australian government has decided to fully privatise its 1,540 km (1,000 mile) Dampier to Bunbury gas pipeline for up to A$1.5 billion, The Australian newspaper reported on Friday.

"The Resources Development and Energy Minister Colin Barnett yesterday told a function hosted by Perth stockbroker Hartley Poynton that the government recognised there were complications in partial privatisation," The Australian said.
Barnett had decided on full privatisation and the proceeds would be used to retire debt, the newspaper said.
The Western Australian government has previously said it wanted to only partially privatise the pipeline.

Barnett said in August last year the government's preferred option at that stage was for a partial privatisation of the pipeline with a 50-50 joint venture between the state-owned AlintaGas and private sector particapants.
Under Barnett's latest plan, which has yet to be approved by the Western Australian cabinet, AlintaGas would be removed as operator and the new owner would have permission to double capacity.

Barnett has criticised a plan from U.S. energy group Pacific Gas & Electric Corp (PG&E) to build a A$1 billion Bunbury to Dampier pipeline, saying it would lower the sale price of the government pipeline.
